summary: This resolution supports designating May 14, 2026, as National Scam Survivor Day and urges greater public awareness of scams, improved access to prevention resources, and collaboration among government, private, and nonprofit groups to support survivors and hold scammers accountable.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is a symbolic measure designating a day for scam awareness. It references federal law enforcement roles and resources but does not authorize, expand, or reduce any government spending or programs. No fiscal implications are present.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue collection.
While the text notes scams targeting veterans through fake VA or health care providers, it does not address healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
No connection to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The resolution does not mention immigration, borders, visas, or related enforcement.
No reference to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affecting military budgets, defense policy, or armed forces spending.
Unrelated to environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation.
No engagement with welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net policies.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No mention of drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

The resolution explicitly supports the role of federal and local law enforcement in discovering, tracking, and halting scam operations and holding scammers accountable. This aligns modestly with tougher enforcement and policing priorities, though the measure is purely symbolic and awareness-focused.
No provisions related to trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No content concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
Unrelated to foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions on voting access, election integrity, or electoral reform.

The text references social media, cryptocurrency, and AI-enabled scams but does not propose new tech regulations, data protections, or privacy rules; it focuses on awareness and existing law enforcement.
No engagement with labor rights, unions, or workplace regulations.
The resolution does not address religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination policy.
